where: Section 2, sentence after the BI/SD formula
problem: The duty cycle is printed as 'SD / BI = 2SO−BO' with no exponent. Read literally this is 2×SO − BO, which is wrong; for BO = 6, SO = 3 a student would get 2×3 − 6 = 0 instead of 1/8. The quiz answer Q6 uses the correct exponent form, so chapter and quiz disagree.
fix: Write it as duty cycle = SD / BI = 2<sup>SO−BO</sup> (two raised to the power SO minus BO), and state that when SO = 3 and BO = 6 this gives 2⁻³ = 1/8 = 12.5 %.

problem: 'The PHY adds 6 bytes around the PSDU' suggests bytes on both sides. All six PHY overhead bytes (preamble, SFD, length) come before the PSDU; nothing is added after it.
fix: The PHY adds 6 bytes before the PSDU: a 4-byte preamble, a 1-byte SFD and a 1-byte length field.

problem: The FCS is drawn as a separate block after the 'MAC frame' block and linked by an arrow from it. The FCS is not extra PHY overhead; it is the last 2 bytes inside the MAC frame. A student may add 2 bytes to the 127-byte PSDU when computing air time.
fix: Show the FCS inside the MAC frame block (for example as 'MAC frame (PSDU), up to 127 B, last 2 B = FCS') so the total on air is 4 + 1 + 1 + 127 = 133 B, not 135 B.

problem: The answer says 127 − 40 = 87 B is left for transport and application. The MAC header (up to 25 bytes) and the 2-byte FCS also sit inside the same 127-byte PSDU, so the real payload left after the IPv6 header is far less than 87 B.
fix: An IPv6 header is 40 B. Inside a 127-B PSDU the MAC header and 2-B FCS already take up to about 27 B, so well under 87 B (roughly 60 B) remains for transport and application data. That tight budget is why 6LoWPAN compresses headers and fragments.

problem: 'This chapter completes the subject' clashes with the chapter's own pointers to Chapter 3.3 (ZigBee) and Chapter 3.5 (6LoWPAN), which come later.
fix: It is the shared radio layer under ZigBee and 6LoWPAN; the next chapters build the upper layers on it.
